WITH line_totals AS (
    SELECT
        l.OrderID,
        CAST(l.Quantity * l.UnitPrice * (1 - COALESCE(l.Discount, 0)) AS DECIMAL(38,4)) AS line_amount
    FROM {{ source('legacy', 'Sales_OrderLines') }} l
),
order_totals AS (
    SELECT
        OrderID,
        SUM(line_amount) AS OrderTotal,
        COUNT(*) AS LineCount
    FROM line_totals
    GROUP BY OrderID
)
SELECT
    o.OrderID,
    o.OrderDate,
    o.Status,
    o.CustomerID,
    t.OrderTotal,
    t.LineCount
FROM {{ source('legacy', 'Sales_Orders') }} o
JOIN order_totals t
    ON t.OrderID = o.OrderID
GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.CustomerID, t.OrderTotal, t.LineCount

explanation: For each order, this procedure adds up the net value of its lines (quantity × unit price, after discount, treating a missing discount as zero) and counts those lines. It returns one row per order for the given customer. Each order's totals depend only on that order's lines, so the customer filter can be applied to the finished rows.
